mainTopic: Whether burning the קומץ creates פיגול for lacking שיריים, and when wrong intentions of half a כזית combine.
overview: The amud opens as רבא finishes a proof from the ברייתא of רבי חייא: burning the קומץ makes even שיריים that became lacking into פיגול. אביי rejects the proof by saying the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר. The גמרא defends this reading by saying the ברייתא is about a מנחת חוטא, and רב דימי's report backs this up. רבא then takes back his own claim, using a ברייתא about a broken loaf of לחם הפנים that he says follows רבי עקיבא. אביי answers that the ברייתא may follow רבי אליעזר instead, so for רבי עקיבא burning could work even when something is missing. A new משנה then teaches that half a כזית of intent to eat and half a כזית of intent to burn do not combine. The גמרא infers from it that two eating intents do combine. It asks how this fits the earlier clause, and רבי ירמיה says the later clause follows רבי אליעזר. אביי offers a different reading that fits the רבנן, and the גמרא challenges it because an earlier משנה already teaches that point.

steps.title: רבא finishes his proof that burning works even for lacking remainder
steps.stepSummary: רבא notes that the ברייתא leaves out 'or a כזית' when it talks about the שיריים, yet still rules פיגול with כרת. This shows that burning the קומץ makes even lacking שיריים into פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he could not teach 'or an olive-bulk' about the remainder, he also did not teach 'or an olive-bulk' in the handful-removal case about eating the remainder. Yet the last part of the ברייתא rules it פיגול, with כרת. So burning works for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is completing his proof. He uses a missing phrase in the ברייתא of רבי חייא to show that the case involves שיריים that became lacking, and that burning still makes them פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds 'or a כזית' in other places but leaves it out when it talks about the שיריים. רבא explains why: those שיריים had already shrunk to about a כזית, so 'or a כזית' would add nothing. Even so, the ברייתא rules פיגול with כרת, so the הקטרה of the קומץ still works on lacking שיריים.

keyTerms.meaning: The remainder of the מנחה left after the קומץ is taken. The כהנים eat it.
Removing a handful (קומץ) of flour from the מנחה.
An olive-bulk, the smallest amount that counts in halacha.
An offering ruined by the intent to eat or burn it after its proper time.
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating פיגול.
Burning the קומץ on the מזבח.

phrases.english: [Since he could not teach] 'or an olive-bulk' about the remainder,
phrases.notes: We're joining רבא mid-sentence. The remainder had shrunk to about a כזית, so adding 'or a כזית' would say nothing new.

phrases.english: in the handful-removal case too, 'to eat the remainder,'
he did not teach 'or an olive-bulk.'
And the last clause teaches:
It is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.
Evidently, burning works for them [even when lacking].
phrases.notes: Burning the קומץ is what normally 'locks in' the פיגול. רבא says it does so even for lacking remainder.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא מַהְנְיָא לְהוּ הַקְטָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's proof, which began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That הקטרה of the קומץ makes lacking שיריים into פיגול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא, which leaves out 'or a כזית' for the שיריים yet rules פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: אביי says the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבא's proof. He says the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר, who holds that offering only a כזית outside the Temple brings no liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: No. Whose view is this? It is רבי אלעזר's. As we learned in a משנה: the קומץ, the לבונה, the קטורת, the מנחת כהנים, the מנחת כהן משיח, and the מנחת נסכים. If one offered a כזית of any of them outside, he is liable. רבי אלעזר exempts him until he offers all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's proof. He suggests a different author for the ברייתא, which gives another reason why the words 'or a כזית' are missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, offering a כזית outside the Temple already brings liability. רבי אלעזר says there is no liability until the whole item is offered. If the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר, then 'a כזית' does not matter for these items. So leaving out 'or a כזית' does not prove the שיריים were lacking.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose view is this?' A way of naming which תנא a source follows.
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח.
Frankincense that goes with the מנחה and is also burned.
Outside the Temple courtyard. Offering there is forbidden.
Exempts from liability.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: No,
whose view is this? It is Rabbi Elazar's,
as we learned: The handful, the frankincense, and the incense,
the meal offering of priests, the meal offering of the anointed priest,
and the meal offering of libations,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהִקְרִיב מֵאַחַת מֵהֶן כְּזַיִת בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: if one offered an olive-bulk of one of them outside, he is liable.
And Rabbi Elazar exempts him
until he offers all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לָא, הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof by assigning the ברייתא to רבי אלעזר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the missing words 'or a כזית'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is another reason the words are missing: according to רבי אלעזר, a כזית does not count for offering outside.

steps.title: אביי explains why 'or an olive-bulk' is left out
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא could not say 'or a כזית of its קומץ outside', it also left out 'or a כזית' for the שיריים, to keep the wording the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since about burning the handful he could not teach 'or an olive-bulk of its handful outside', about the remainder he also did not teach 'or an olive-bulk.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his rejection. He gives his own reason why the ברייתא never says 'or a כזית'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, intending to burn only a כזית of the קומץ outside means nothing. So the ברייתא could not write 'or a כזית' there. To keep the two clauses matching, it also left it out for the שיריים. That has nothing to do with the שיריים being lacking.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because.
He could not teach it. It could not be included in the wording.

phrases.english: Since regarding burning the handful

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִתְּנֵי לֵיהּ ״אוֹ כְּזַיִת מִקּוּמְצָהּ בַּחוּץ״,
phrases.english: he could not teach 'or an olive-bulk of its handful outside,'
regarding the remainder as well
he did not teach 'or an olive-bulk.'

steps.whatToRemember: רבא reads the missing 'or a כזית' as a sign that the שיריים were lacking. אביי says it is missing only because the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּבְהַקְטָרַת קְמִיצָה לָא מִתְּנֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אלעזר's view to the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's reading of the missing phrase.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase is missing to keep the wording uniform, not because the שיריים were lacking.

steps.title: If it follows רבי אלעזר, the frankincense should be mentioned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי. If the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר, it should say 'to burn its קומץ and its לבונה', because רבי אלעזר requires both together for liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי אלעזר, then 'to burn its handful' should have said 'to burn its handful and its frankincense'. As we learned: the handful and the frankincense, if one offered one of them outside, he is liable. רבי אלעזר exempts him until he offers both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's claim that the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that there is no liability for offering the קומץ outside until the לבונה is offered with it. So by his view, intent to burn only the קומץ outside should not count. The ברייתא, though, mentions only the קומץ, which does not fit רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: If.
It should have said. Used to point out wording that seems wrong.
Both of them.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Elazar,
this phrase 'to burn its handful'
should have said 'to burn its handful and its frankincense!'
As we learned: The handful and the frankincense,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהִקְרִיב אֶת אֶחָד מֵהֶן בַּחוּץ – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: if one offered one of them outside, he is liable.
And Rabbi Elazar exempts him
until he offers both of them.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two משניות. The first is about a כזית versus the whole item. This one is about the קומץ alone versus the קומץ together with the לבונה.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, הַאי לְהַקְטִיר קוּמְצָהּ, לְהַקְטִיר קוּמְצָהּ וּלְבוֹנָתָהּ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's claim that the author is רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר requires both the קומץ and the לבונה for liability, yet the ברייתא mentions only the קומץ.

steps.title: The ברייתא is talking about a sinner's מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא only needs to teach the case of the קומץ of a מנחת חוטא, which has no לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא was only needed for the handful of a sinner's meal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. The ברייתא never mentions לבונה because it is talking about a מנחת חוטא, which has no לבונה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says you are only liable when the whole מתיר is offered outside. In a regular מנחה that means the קומץ and the לבונה together. In a מנחת חוטא the קומץ alone is the whole מתיר, so the ברייתא can say just 'its קומץ'. A כזית of it is still not enough, so the ברייתא still leaves out 'or a כזית'.

keyTerms.meaning: It was only needed for... (narrows a teaching to one specific case)
A sinner's meal offering, brought by a poor person for certain sins. It has no oil and no לבונה.
The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
The part of an offering whose service permits the rest to be eaten

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְקוֹמֶץ דְּמִנְחַת חוֹטֵא.
phrases.english: It is needed only for the handful of a sinner's meal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 so that אביי's reading can stand.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about an ordinary מנחה, so under רבי אלעזר it should have said 'its קומץ and its לבונה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a מנחת חוטא, where the קומץ alone is the full מתיר.

steps.title: Would the תנא go to such trouble for one narrow case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether the תנא would really bother to teach a law that only fits a sinner's מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did the תנא really go to all that trouble just to teach us about the handful of a sinner's meal offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. It doubts that a general teaching would be about such a narrow case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a teaching about פיגול in מנחות is meant to cover all kinds of מנחות. Saying it only fits a מנחת חוטא makes the ברייתא very narrow. So the גמרא asks whether that answer is really believable.

keyTerms.meaning: Went to the trouble, made the effort
To teach us, to let us hear

phrases.english: And did the תנא go to all that trouble to teach us
the handful of a sinner's meal offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכְּפֵל תַּנָּא לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how believable the answer in step 5 is.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is only about a מנחת חוטא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is unlikely that a תנא would phrase a teaching so that it fits only one rare kind of מנחה.

steps.title: Yes, and רב דימי reports the same reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, and supports this with רב דימי's report that רבי אלעזר also explained the teaching as being about a sinner's מנחה, following the תנא רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. And so too, when רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי אלעזר: it is the handful of a sinner's meal offering, and it follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the תנא really did go to that trouble. It then shows that an אמורא from ארץ ישראל explained the teaching the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not just a forced way out. רב דימי reports that the אמורא רבי אלעזר also read the teaching as being about a מנחת חוטא, matching the view of the תנא רבי אלעזר. This exactly backs up אביי's approach.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
And similarly, introducing support from another source
'It is' — this teaching follows the view of a certain sage

steps.confusionAlert: There are two people named רבי אלעזר here. The one who 'said' is the אמורא, רבי אלעזר בן פדת. The one in 'ורבי אלעזר היא' is the תנא whose view the ברייתא follows.

phrases.english: Yes.
And similarly, when רב דימי came
he said that רבי אלעזר said:
It is the handful of a sinner's meal offering,
and it follows רבי אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין. וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and supports step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the narrow reading and backing it with a report
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A תנא would not teach something that applies only to a מנחת חוטא.
steps.terutzMaskana: He did, and רב דימי's report of רבי אלעזר confirms this reading.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's defense holds: the ברייתא follows the תנא רבי אלעזר and is about a מנחת חוטא, so it cannot prove רבא's point.

steps.title: רבא takes back his own idea because of לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: רבא says his earlier claim was wrong, and brings a ברייתא: if one loaf of לחם הפנים broke, all the loaves are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then רבא said: What I said is nothing. For it was taught: 'It is most holy' — this teaches that if one of the loaves broke, all its loaves are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes back what he said in step 1, that burning the קומץ makes even שיריים that became too small into פיגול. He starts his proof with a ברייתא about לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הוא' in the פסוק teaches that the לחם הפנים must stay whole. If one loaf breaks, burning the bowls of לבונה cannot permit any of the loaves. This hints that the burning does not work on something broken or lacking, and the next step completes the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Then he went back (changed his mind)
It is nothing, it is not correct
The showbread, twelve loaves placed on the שולחן in the היכל
Broke, was split into pieces

phrases.english: Then רבא said:
What I said is nothing,
phrases.notes: He is taking back his claim from step 1 about שיריים that became too small.

phrases.english: as it is taught: 'It is most holy,'
that if one of them broke,
all of its loaves are disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אביי discussion and goes back to רבא's own claim from step 1 to reject it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's own claim that burning the קומץ makes שיריים that became too small into פיגול
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows that something broken or lacking is not helped by the burning of the מתיר.

steps.title: Even רבי עקיבא agrees a broken item is not helped
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא: a loaf that went outside does not ruin the rest. That fits רבי עקיבא, who says זריקה works for what went out. Yet even he says it does not work for a broken loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if one went out, those that are inside are fit. Whom have you heard who says that זריקה works for something that went out? It is רבי עקיבא. And still he says that if it broke, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his proof. He shows the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, the sage most generous about what the service can cover, and even he says it does not help a broken item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only disqualifies the loaves when one broke, not when one went out. So it holds that the service helps the loaves left inside. That is רבי עקיבא's view, that זריקה works even for what went out. If even he says a broken loaf is not helped, then burning the קומץ certainly cannot make שיריים that became too small into פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Went out (of the area where it must stay)
Inside
Throwing the blood on the מזבח, the service that permits the offering
Works for the item that went out

steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבא's case for taking back his claim from step 1. If it holds, burning the קומץ cannot make שיריים that became too small into פיגול. אביי challenges this proof in the next steps.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's claim: going out and becoming broken are different. Even רבי עקיבא, who lets the service cover an item that went out, would not let it cover a broken or lacking item. אביי disputes this reading of the ברייתא in steps 10-13.

phrases.english: But if it went out,
those that are inside are fit.
Whom have you heard who says:
The זריקה works for what went out?
It is רבי עקיבא.
And yet he says: if it broke, no.
phrases.notes: He means the burning does not help a broken loaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא יָצָאת – הָנֵי דְּאִיכָּא גַּוַּואי כְּשֵׁרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof that step 8 began.
steps.raayaObject: Burning the מתיר does not affect an item that is broken or lacking, so רבא's claim in step 1 is wrong.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on לחם הפנים, shown to follow רבי עקיבא, who is generous about זריקה for an item that went out but not for a broken one.

steps.title: אביי: maybe the ברייתא implies something else
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא's reading. The ברייתא never says that a loaf that went out leaves the rest כשר. Maybe it implies that if one loaf became impure, the rest are כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Does the ברייתא actually say 'but if one went out, the rest are fit'? Maybe what it implies is: but if one became impure, the others are fit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's proof from step 9. He says the ברייתא can be read differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed the hidden contrast in the ברייתא was 'broken = all פסול, but went out = the rest are fine.' אביי suggests the hidden contrast is really 'broken = all פסול, but impure = the rest are fine.' If so, the ברייתא says nothing about a loaf that went out, and רבא's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: It went out of its proper area (the courtyard)
It became ritually impure
Valid, still fit to use (said of the remaining loaves)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not quoting a different ברייתא. He is offering a different way to fill in what the same ברייתא leaves unsaid.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבא, who brought the proof in step 9.

phrases.english: Does it teach 'but if one went out' [the rest are fit]?
Perhaps: but if one became impure,
those [remaining loaves] are fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי קָתָנֵי הָא יָצָאת? דִּלְמָא הָא נִטְמֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference רבא drew from the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof itself. It does not prove the opposite position.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed that 'went out' was the implied contrast case. It could just as well be 'became impure.'

steps.title: Why impurity is different: the ציץ
steps.stepSummary: An impure loaf does not ruin the rest because the ציץ makes up for impurity. A loaf that went out does ruin the rest, so the ברייתא would follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the ציץ effects acceptance for impurity. But if a loaf went out, no. And the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who says sprinkling does not help for something that went out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the logic of his alternate reading. He also says which תנא the ברייתא would then follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ of the כהן גדול makes up for טומאה, so an impure loaf does not ruin the others. Nothing makes up for a loaf that went out, so it ruins the rest just like a broken one does. That fits רבי אליעזר, who holds that זריקה does not help for something that left, and not רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden headplate worn by the כהן גדול
Makes an offering acceptable despite a flaw
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח (or the parallel act that permits an offering)
Is not effective
An item that left its proper area

steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the ברייתא over to רבי אליעזר. That frees רבי עקיבא from the conclusion רבא tried to pin on him.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the ציץ effects acceptance [for impurity],
but [if one] went out, no.
phrases.notes: He means that when a loaf went out, all the loaves are פסול, the same as when one breaks.

phrases.english: And it is [the view of] Rabbi Eliezer,
who says: sprinkling is not effective for what went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? דִּמְרַצֵּה צִיץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind אביי's alternate reading from step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Recasts the ברייתא as the view of רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא's proof only works if the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, and it may not.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא mentions a broken loaf
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really should also have mentioned a loaf that went out. It chose a broken loaf to teach that even when the piece is still inside, הקטרה does not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: By right it should also have taught 'went out.' The reason it taught 'broke' is to teach us that even if it broke, so it is still inside, burning does not help it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers a question nobody asked out loud: if 'went out' also ruins everything, why did the ברייתא only mention 'broke'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under אביי's reading, both 'broke' and 'went out' make all the loaves פסול. The ברייתא picked 'broke' because it is the bigger חידוש: the loaf is still inside the עזרה, and even so הקטרה cannot fix it.

keyTerms.meaning: By right, properly
It broke
It teaches us (the new point)
Inside (the Temple courtyard)
Burning on the מזבח, here the act that permits the loaves

phrases.english: And by right it should have
also taught 'went out' [makes all פסול],
and the fact that it teaches 'broke' —
this it teaches us:
that even if it broke, where it is still inside,
burning does not help it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְדִין הוּא דְּאִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְמִיתְנֵי נָמֵי יָצָאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends אביי's reading against a hidden question about the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the ברייתא chose one example over the other (a bigger חידוש).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If 'went out' also ruins everything, the ברייתא should have said so.
steps.terutzMaskana: It picked 'broke' to show that even an item still inside cannot be fixed by הקטרה.

steps.title: For רבי עקיבא, burning helps even when something is missing
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי עקיבא, who says זריקה helps for an item that went out, הקטרה also helps when something is missing. רבא's proof is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי עקיבא, who says sprinkling is effective for what went out, even for something missing, burning helps.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his argument. He states what רבי עקיבא would hold, which is the opposite of what רבא claimed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that even רבי עקיבא agrees that a missing piece cannot be fixed. אביי shows that the ברייתא can be read as following רבי אליעזר. If so, it says nothing about רבי עקיבא, who could hold that הקטרה works even in a case of חסרון.

keyTerms.meaning: Something missing, an incomplete measure
Is effective, helps

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: the broken-loaf ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר. For רבי עקיבא, הקטרה helps even for חסרון, so רבא's retraction proof fails.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Akiva,
who says: sprinkling is effective for what went out,
even [for] something missing as well,
burning helps it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּאָמַר: זְרִיקָה מוֹעֶלֶת לַיּוֹצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion of אביי's rejection.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי עקיבא, הקטרה works even for a missing piece. The ברייתא of the broken loaf follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: New משנה: half a זית of eating and half a זית of burning do not combine
steps.stepSummary: If a person intended to eat half a זית and burn half a זית at the wrong time or place, the offering stays כשר, because eating and burning do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: [If one intended] to eat half an olive-bulk and to burn half an olive-bulk [improperly], it is fit, because eating and burning do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches a rule about wrong intentions that are split between eating and burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wrong intention only makes an offering פסול if it covers a full כזית. Here each intention is only half a זית. Eating and burning are different kinds of acts, so the two halves are not added together, and the offering stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, our משנה
About half an olive-bulk
Join together, combine into one amount

phrases.english: MISHNA:
[If one intended] to eat half an olive-bulk
phrases.notes: He means intending to eat or burn it outside the proper time or place. The intention is the problem, not actually eating it.

phrases.english: and to burn half an olive-bulk, it is fit,
because eating and burning do not join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶאֱכוֹל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וּלְהַקְטִיר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half a זית of wrong intention about eating plus half a זית about burning does not make the offering פסול, because eating and burning do not combine.

steps.title: Reading the משנה closely: two eatings do combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the משנה blocks combining only between eating and burning. Two eatings combine, even if one is of an item not normally eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason the halves do not combine is that one was eating and one was burning. So if he planned to eat half a זית of the leftover and to eat half a זית of something not normally eaten, they do combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion by reading the משנה from Step 14 closely and drawing an inference from its wording. This sets up the problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the offering stays כשר because eating and burning do not combine. So the problem is only mixing two different kinds of action. If both plans are 'eating', they should combine into a full זית, even when one half is the קומץ, which normally goes on the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason; the גמרא is pointing to exactly why the משנה rules this way
Combines; two half-amounts join to make a full זית
An item not normally eaten, such as the קומץ that is burned on the altar
But this implies; it introduces an inference from the משנה's wording

phrases.english: GEMARA: The reason is that it was to eat and to burn,
but if it was to eat and to eat
an item not normally eaten, it combines.
phrases.notes: He means the קומץ. It normally goes on the altar, but here he planned to eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלֶאֱכוֹל וּלְהַקְטִיר, הָא לֶאֱכוֹל וְלֶאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the משנה quoted in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By implication, plans to eat two half-זיתים combine, even when one half is something not normally eaten.

steps.title: The first clause counts only items normally eaten
steps.stepSummary: The earlier clause of the משנה makes only intent about an item normally eaten count. So the inference from Step 15 clashes with it. Who taught the later clause?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first clause teaches: to eat something normally eaten, or to burn something normally burned. So intent about something normally eaten counts, and intent about something not normally eaten does not. Who taught this later part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a contradiction between the earlier clause of the משנה and the inference from Step 15. It asks which תנא could hold the later clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause gives the rule for wrong intent: eating what is normally eaten, burning what is normally burned. So a plan to eat the קומץ should mean nothing at all. If it means nothing, it cannot combine with another half-זית, yet Step 15 implied that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
An item normally eaten, such as the leftover of a מנחה that the כהנים eat
Yes... no; it marks what is included and what is left out
Which תנא taught this? It asks whose opinion this part of the משנה follows

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not that two halves never combine. It is that intent about the קומץ should not count at all, so there is nothing there to combine.

phrases.english: But the first clause teaches:
to eat an item that is normally eaten,
or to burn an item that is normally burned,
an item normally eaten, yes;
one that is not normally eaten, no.
Who taught this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָקָתָנֵי רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference from Step 15 using the earlier clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that eating something not normally eaten combines
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause counts only intent about items normally eaten. So intent to eat the קומץ means nothing and cannot combine. The two clauses seem to follow different opinions.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: this follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the later clause follows רבי אליעזר. He holds that wrong intent can cross over between a person's eating and the altar's 'eating'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי אליעזר. He says wrong intent can move from a person's eating to the altar, and from the altar's eating to a person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question by naming the תנא behind the later clause: רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, planning to eat the קומץ or to burn the leftover is real wrong intent, even though each belongs to the 'other side'. So for him a plan to eat the קומץ does count, and it can combine with a plan to eat the leftover. The first clause, by contrast, follows the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
One can have intent that affects the offering
A person's eating, meaning the parts the כהנים eat
The altar's 'eating', meaning the parts that are burned

steps.whatToRemember: The two clauses follow different תנאים. The first follows the רבנן, and the later clause, where eating something not normally eaten combines, follows רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Whose opinion is this?
It is Rabbi Eliezer, who says:
one can have intent from a person's eating to the altar,
phrases.notes: Like planning to burn the leftover, which the כהנים normally eat.

phrases.english: and from the altar's eating to a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by naming the תנא of the later clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the clause to a different תנא (רבי אליעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה follows one view, so intent about something not normally eaten should never count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later clause follows רבי אליעזר, for whom intent can cross over between a person's eating and the altar's.

steps.title: The source: רבי אליעזר disqualifies the מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה showing that רבי אליעזר disqualifies a מנחה when the intent is to eat what is not normally eaten, or to burn what is not normally burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: One who takes the קומץ from a מנחה planning to eat something not normally eaten, or to burn something not normally burned, the מנחה is כשר. רבי אליעזר disqualifies it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי ירמיה by quoting the משנה where רבי אליעזר's view appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says this 'crossed' intent does nothing, so the מנחה is כשר. רבי אליעזר rules it פסול, which shows that for him such intent counts. That is why, by his view, it can join with another half-זית of eating.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who takes the handful (קומץ) from the מנחה
A flour offering
Rules the offering unfit

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר rules the מנחה פסול, but it is not פיגול, so there is no כרת for eating it.

phrases.english: As we learned: One who takes a handful from the meal offering
to eat an item that is not normally eaten,
phrases.notes: Here that means the קומץ, eaten after its proper time.

phrases.english: or to burn an item that is not normally burned,
phrases.notes: Here that means the leftover of the מנחה, which the כהנים normally eat.

phrases.english: it is fit, and Rabbi Eliezer rules it unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַקּוֹמֵץ אֶת הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבי אליעזר quoted in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds intent can cross over between a person's eating and the altar's
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 17a, where רבי אליעזר disqualifies a מנחה over such intent

steps.title: אביי: The Later Clause Can Follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the later clause can follow the רבנן. The inference is not about an item not normally eaten. It is about two eatings where both items are normally eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say the משנה follows the רבנן. Don't read the inference as 'eating plus eating something not normally eaten.' Read it as 'eating plus eating something that is normally eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer to the problem from Step 16. He keeps the משנה in line with the רבנן by changing what we infer from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15 we inferred that two eatings combine 'even if one is of an item not normally eaten,' and that clashed with the earlier clause. אביי says the inference is narrower: two eating intents combine only when both are about items normally eaten. With that reading, there is no clash and no need to say the clause follows רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. Introduces an answer that works even for the view we thought it couldn't fit.
The Rabbis, who disagree with רבי אליעזר here
Don't say this, rather say that. Re-reads what the text implies.
An item that is normally eaten

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not changing the words of the משנה. He is changing what we infer from it, which was the inference made in Step 15.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
You can even say it follows the Rabbis.
Don't say that this means

phrases.aramaic: לֶאֱכוֹל וְלֶאֱכוֹל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל,
phrases.english: to eat, and to eat an item not normally eaten,
rather, say that this means
to eat, and to eat an item that is normally eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אביי אמר אפילו תימא רבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of Step 16, instead of רבי ירמיה's answer in Steps 17-18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the inference from the משנה so it matches the רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later clause implies that eating an item not normally eaten combines with regular eating, so it must follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later clause only implies that two eatings of normally-eaten items combine, so it can follow the רבנן.

steps.title: Why Teach This? An Earlier משנה Already Says It
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: if the clause only teaches that two normal eatings combine, an earlier משנה already says so outright, listing half-זית intents outside and the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is it teaching us? It is already taught explicitly: if he intended to eat a זית outside and a זית tomorrow, or a זית tomorrow and a זית outside, or half a זית outside and half a זית tomorrow, or half a זית tomorrow and half a זית outside, the offering is פסול, but there is no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's reading by saying it makes the clause pointless. It quotes an earlier משנה that already teaches this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the clause teaches that two half-זית eating intents combine. But the earlier משנה already rules that half a זית outside its place plus half a זית after its time make the offering פסול. So the clause would be repeating a known rule, and a משנה is not supposed to repeat itself for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? A challenge that something seems to add nothing new.
Explicitly, outright
Outside its proper place
Tomorrow, past its proper time
The punishment of being cut off, which comes with true פיגול

phrases.english: And what is it teaching us?
But it is already taught explicitly:
to eat an olive-bulk outside
and an olive-bulk tomorrow,
an olive-bulk tomorrow and an olive-bulk outside,

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר,
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk outside and half an olive-bulk tomorrow,

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ –
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk tomorrow and half an olive-bulk outside,
it is unfit, but there is no karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: ומאי קא משמע לן הא בהדיא קתני לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer from Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that the later clause teaches that two normal eatings combine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under אביי, the clause adds nothing new. An earlier משנה already says outright that two half-זית eating intents combine to make the offering פסול.
